To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
early changes in contrast-enhanced CT of pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor liver metastases may be used as a surrogate for outcome in PRRT.

the contrast enhancement of liver metastases of PNET patients receiving PRRT with 177Lu-DOATATE correlated with the PFS and time to best treatment response, suggesting that CECT could be used for monitoring of PRRT.

the contrast-enhancement in liver metastases from pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors increased after 3–5 PRRT cycles, and that this increase in contrast-enhancement correlated with progression-free survival.

the development and application of a novel method for monitoring of 177Lu-DOTA-octreotate (177Lu-DOTATE), a radiopharmaceutical that is used for treatment of neuroendocrine tumors.

the contrast-enhancement of PNET metastases increased slightly during PRRT and that this increase correlated with outcome parameters such as PFS and time to best tumor response.

The main takeaway from our work is that
CECT monitoring of 177Lu-DOTA-TATE treatment in PNET patients is feasible, and may be used for early evaluation of response and for identification of non-responders.
the contrast-enhancement of liver metastases of PNETs is increased in the early stages of PRRT and that the increase in tumor contrast-enhancement may correlate with PFS and time to best-response.
